import_alexa_media.title: Borrow from Alexa Media Player
import_alexa_media.description: Reuse the Amazon sign-in that Alexa Media Player already holds, with no second sign-in and no new device registration. That integration keeps working; sharing the token does not disturb its session.

import_token.title: Use an existing credential bundle
import_token.description: Paste a credential bundle from an account that is already registered. It must contain the refresh token, macDms and device serial. The marketplace below is only used if the bundle does not name one.

login_password.title: Sign in with email, password and 2FA key
login_password.description:
Enter the same details you would give Alexa Media Player. A window then opens on Amazon's own sign-in with your email and password already filled in, and if you also give the authenticator app key from Amazon's 2-step verification, the one-time code is filled in too, so you only click through.

Nothing typed here is saved. Once you are signed in only the refresh token is kept, and the password and key are discarded.

To get the key: on Amazon go to Login & security, 2-step verification, Add new app, then choose "Can't scan the barcode?" and copy the 52-character key shown. This path is new and has not yet been tried against a live account.

data.otp_secret: Authenticator app key for Amazon 2-step verification (optional)
data.hass_url: Home Assistant URL (as your browser reaches it)

data_description.otp_secret: The 52-character key, for example 35T5 LQSY I5IO 3EFQ LGAJ I6YB JWBY JJPR PYT7 XPPW IDAK SQBJ CVXA. Spaces are fine. Leave empty to type the code yourself.
data_description.hass_url: The sign-in window is served by Home Assistant at this address, so it must be one your browser can open.

proxy_warning.title: Home Assistant cannot reach that URL

data.proxy_warning: Continue anyway. My browser can reach this URL even though Home Assistant cannot.

totp_register.title: Check the one-time code
totp_register.description:
**{email} on {url}**

The authenticator key you gave produces this code right now, valid for another {seconds} seconds:

> **{code}**

Compare it with the code in your authenticator app, or with the one Amazon showed when you added the app. If it matches, tick the box and continue. If it does not, the key was copied wrong: go back and paste it again. Submitting with the box unticked shows a fresh code.

login.title: Sign in to Amazon with a blank form (not working yet)
login.description: This path is unfinished and is not expected to succeed. Amazon answers a new device registration with a challenge whose page will not load through the sign-in relay, so it stops partway. Use one of the other options instead; the one above fills the same form in for you the way Alexa Media Player does. If you want to try this anyway: after you submit, a window opens for Amazon's own sign-in, and the Home Assistant URL below must be the one your browser can reach.

data.hass_url: Home Assistant URL (as your browser reaches it)

select_devices.title: Choose devices
select_devices.description: {count} devices on your Amazon account can be added to Home Assistant. You can change this later without signing in again.

devices_pick.title: Choose devices
devices_pick.description: Tick each of the {count} devices you want in Home Assistant: one entity per Alexa feature (switch, select, number, sensor, lock), exactly as Alexa reports it. Nothing is assembled here; build fans and other whole devices from these entities in Kitbash.

data_description.include_endpoints: One entity per feature, nothing assembled.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate with Amazon
reauth_confirm.description: Your stored credentials are no longer accepted. Choose how to sign in again; your existing configuration and devices are kept.

error.login_failed: Login did not complete. Make sure you finished Amazon's sign-in, and try from a browser not already signed in to Amazon. If you gave an authenticator key, check the code it produces matches your app.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Amazon. Check your connection and try again.
error.invalid_bundle: That is not a usable credential bundle. It must be JSON containing refreshToken, macDms and deviceSerial.
error.invalid_auth: Amazon rejected those credentials. The refresh token may have been revoked.
error.2fa_key_invalid: That is not a valid authenticator key. It should be the 52-character key Amazon shows when you add an authenticator app: letters A to Z and digits 2 to 7, spaces allowed.

abort.already_configured: This Amazon account is already set up.
abort.proxy_missing: The login session was lost. Start again.
abort.no_alexa_media: No Alexa Media Player account with a stored sign-in was found.
abort.wrong_account: That sign-in was for a different Amazon account. Sign in with the account this entry was set up for.
